concepts.why: The patient has a history of biopsy-proven psoriasis and presents with scaly erythematous plaques on the lateral leg.
The patient has a history of juvenile dermatomyositis and presents with violaceous to erythematous patches on the joints, periungual skin, and chest.

The patient presents with diffuse ill-defined erythema and mild edema of the face and eyelids, and increased erythema on chest, dorsal hands, and eyelids, which may be related to an autoimmune process.
The patient reports difficulty picking up her child and climbing stairs, which may indicate muscle weakness, and has a history of juvenile dermatomyositis.
The patient presents with photodistributed poikiloderma on the chest, which is a characteristic skin finding.
The patient presents with a combination of skin and joint findings, which may be suggestive of systemic lupus erythematosus.
The patient reports difficulty picking up her child and climbing stairs, which may indicate joint inflammation, and has a history of autoimmune disorders.
The patient presents with a combination of skin and joint findings, which may be suggestive of Sjögren's syndrome.
